head: Printed and catalogued sources this archive has actually opened
lede: Record sets above are databases. These are books and catalogues — every one free, out of copyright or open without an account, every one read rather than cited. They are listed here because until 15 September 2026 each of them lived only on the one or two pages that happened to use it.
rows: Whitworth Porter, History of the Corps of Royal Engineers, vol. 1

Lieutenant Robert D'Arcy at the siege of Fort St Philip's, Minorca, 1781; «Robert D'Arcy, Barbados» in a station list; Commanding Engineer at Copenhagen 1807; Commanding Royal Engineer at Walcheren 1809 and the arrest at Flushing.
NOTHING, and the null is controlled: the volume mentions the Peninsula 48 times, Waterloo 11 and the Crimea 43. It is the post-1815 volume and his service ended about 1809.

The seniority chain that settles 17 JANUARY 1776 in three separate editions; Second Lieutenant in 1783, Captain of the Royal Engineers by 1802, Major in the army by 1803; and «D'Arcy, Lt. Col. Joseph, Royal Art.» in 1821. Also the spelling ROBERT D'ARCEY, which is why outside catalogues had never returned him.
All three D'Arcys in one place, 17 January 1776 confirmed, and the Persia service moved from inferred to documented.
Connolly's Roll of Officers of the Corps of Royal Engineers
Entry 203, the full career and «Died at Chatham, 13 5 1827». Only two D'Arcys in the whole Roll. It carries no parentage — the Roll does not record fathers.
A structural silence about 1776, and one exact date: by warrant of 23 April 1787, issue 12850 page 197, the Corps of Engineers became the Corps of ROYAL Engineers.
John Smyth of Nibley, A Description of the Hundred of Berkeley
written c. 1639, printed 1885 as vol. 3 of The Berkeley Manuscripts

«Swonhunger; corruptly called Saniger», and three further and flatter alias statements in the language of an estate survey; the hamlets of Hamfallow; and the freehold called OLDMINSTER with its own tithe barn, which reappears in a deed of 1690–1741.
Smyth, The Lives of the Berkeleys
The Swonhunger pedigree, six generations to the failure of the main line in 1401 and the estate's passage to Thorpe.
Isaac Herbert Jeayes, Descriptive Catalogue of the Charters and Muniments at Berkeley Castle
The Berkeley charters itemised — including a fishery reserved on Wednesdays and Fridays.
Samuel Rudder, A New History of Gloucestershire

A controlled null — the hamlet is absent from 5.7 million characters while Wanswell, Hamfallow, Halmore and Alkington are all in his index — and the Thorps of Wanswell holding by castle-guard at a named tower, carried to 1525.
Ralph Bigland, Historical, Monumental and Genealogical Collections relative to the County of Gloucester
«Saniger, long held by an old Family of the same Name»; the Berkeley monuments; and Edward Saniger among the freeholders of Hinton.
John Smyth, Men and Armour for Gloucestershire in 1608
Eleven men of the surname, with trade, age and stature — and a printer's error this archive published for a day. See the next row.
The contemporary review of that 1902 edition, listing its misreadings: «Thus SAINGER SHOULD READ SANIGER.» Three spellings in 1608, not four. Correction 31.

195 records under the medieval spellings of the surname against 71 under the modern one; the Berkeley Castle Muniments calendared item by item; the Awre manor court rolls, 1387 to 1881; the E 179 hearth taxes; and the Protestation Returns series, from which Gloucestershire is missing.
note: Fourteen sources, and not one of them cost anything. Two are on this list for what they did NOT contain, because a controlled null is a result — and one is here for an error it found in this archive rather than a fact it gave.
